source_text: Qua igitur fronte subiungis: Sed " per unum hominem peccatum in mundum intravit, et per peccatum mors; et ita in omnes homines pertransiit, in quo omnes peccaverunt [n49] "? Quod interpretaris hoc modo, ut peccatum ab illo dicat Apostolus generatione in posteros fuisse transmissum [n50] . Supra concesseras Magistrum Gentium nuptias, quibus Deus benedixerat, nihil accusare; voluntatem ad peccandum in nascente non esse; parentes autem, in quantum parentes sunt, licite sibi legitimeque ad procreandos filios coniugari; et addis illico, quasi dormiens priora dixisses, crimen ad posteros generatione transmitti. Si enim in tantum generant, in quantum parentes sunt; in quantum autem parentes sunt, licite sibi et legitime iunguntur; et haec coniunctio ab Apostolo non improbatur, quia a Deo non solum instituta, verum etiam benedicta est; quo ore, qua lege, qua fronte, hanc generationem reatus causam, radice criminum, servam diaboli, esse confirmas?
pass_a_gloss: With what forehead, therefore, do you subjoin: But 'through one human being sin entered into the world, and through sin death; and so it passed through into all human beings, in whom all sinned'? Which you interpret in this way, that the Apostle says sin was transmitted from that man into posterity by generation. Above you had granted that the Teacher of the Gentiles accuses marriages, which God had blessed, in nothing; that a will toward sinning is not in the one being born; but that parents, insofar as they are parents, are joined to themselves licitly and legitimately toward procreating children; and you add at once, as if sleeping you had said the earlier things, that a crime is transmitted to posterity by generation. For if they generate only insofar as they are parents; but insofar as they are parents they are joined to themselves licitly and legitimately; and this conjunction is not disapproved by the Apostle, because it has been not only instituted by God but also blessed; with what mouth, by what law, with what forehead do you confirm that this generation is a cause of reatus, a root of crimes, a slave of the devil?

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: With what effrontery, then, do you add: ‘But through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin; and so it passed into all human beings, in whom all sinned’ (Romans 5:12)? You interpret this to mean that the apostle says sin was transmitted from that man to his descendants by generation (Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.45). Above, you had conceded that the Teacher of the Gentiles does not accuse marriage, which God blessed; that no will to sin exists in the newborn child; and that parents, insofar as they are parents, are lawfully and legitimately united to produce children. Immediately you add, as though you had said the earlier things in your sleep, that guilt is transmitted to descendants by generation. If they beget only insofar as they are parents, and insofar as they are parents are lawfully and legitimately united, and this union is not disapproved by the apostle because God not only instituted but also blessed it, with what mouth, by what rule, with what effrontery do you maintain that this generation is the cause of guilt, a root of crimes, and the devil’s slave?

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Parents insofar as parents are not guilty; keep the forensic 'in quantum parentes sunt'.
